v.rationale: Both implementations find the same four root causes and fix them in nearly the same way: remove the try/catch and add failed(), add an atomic claim with a stale TTL plus an idempotency guard, use withoutOverlapping(10), and replace chunk() with chunkById(). Both pass their own suites. Probes on both (real database worker: outage ends in failed_jobs, outage then recovery, two queued copies of a job make one CRM call, deleted subscriber) behaved correctly. Neither has a real bug. impl-1 uses more modern queue attributes and a careful Tries/MaxExceptions/releaseAfter combination, but that is more ceremony than needed. It also adds DeleteWhenMissingModels, which the task did not ask for, and its key failed_jobs claim is backed only by a throw assertion, a manual failed() call and a reflection test of attribute values. impl-2 is simpler and proves fix 1 end to end with a real queue worker. It adds global preventStrayRequests and keeps its new tests in their own file. The ranking is narrow and goes to impl-2 on test quality and simplicity.
